item.title: Tree blocking access to my drive, 16th August
item.description:
I am writing to formally request urgent action regarding the council-owned tree located at the entrance to my driveway at 84 Reddings Road, Cheltenham. Over recent years, the tree has grown significantly, and its expanding root system is now actively lifting the tarmac surrounding its base. This ground displacement has created a severe vehicle clearance issue and a structural hazard at the sole point of access to my property. The physical restriction is now critical. When my neighbor has a vehicle parked on their adjacent driveway, maneuvering around the raised tarmac and tree trunk is exceptionally difficult. Continued root growth will very shortly render my driveway entirely inaccessible by car. Furthermore, the uneven, buckling tarmac poses an immediate trip hazard and risks causing damage to vehicles. Given that the tree is severely compromising safe, unhindered vehicular access to my private residence, I request that an officer inspect the site as a matter of priority to determine an appropriate solution—such as root management, resurfacing, or removal. I have attached a photograph clearly showing the extent of the tarmac displacement and the resulting access obstruction. I look forward to hearing from you regarding a date for an inspection.

item.title: Herd of wild horses out of control, 16th August
item.description:
There is a herd of wild horses roaming the footpaths in Nutterwood above Nutters cottage. They are skewbald and piebald. Yesterday morning at 8.40am I was descending through the wood with my Labrador who was on a lead. I met the horses and the point where the path in the woods meets the common land and they started to walk towards us and chased us through the edge of the wood cantering and some galloping from where they were grazing. I had to let my dog off the lead and make him run ahead as I was afraid one or both of us were going to get trampled as we had no where safe to go other than under the barbed wire where the wood is sectioned off. I would urge you to take this seriously as this is the second time in two weeks they have done this to me and I grew up around horses so I’m generally not bothered by horses on a public bridleway or footpath. I was going to report this to 101 but they are only interested in animals on the highway.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Tewkesbury
